name: mkldnn_reorder_conv3d_weight
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::mkldnn_reorder_conv3d_weight(Tensor self, SymInt[3] padding=[0, 0, 0], SymInt[3] stride=[1, 1, 1], SymInt[3] dilation=[1, 1, 1], SymInt groups=1, SymInt[]? input_size=None) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract; do not narrow tests to this signature. All registered schemas for this operator are: aten::mkldnn_reorder_conv3d_weight(Tensor self, SymInt[3] padding=[0, 0, 0], SymInt[3] stride=[1, 1, 1], SymInt[3] dilation=[1, 1, 1], SymInt groups=1, SymInt[]? input_size=None) -> Tensor ; aten::mkldnn_reorder_conv3d_weight.out(Tensor self, SymInt[3] padding=[0, 0, 0], SymInt[3] stride=[1, 1, 1], SymInt[3] dilation=[1, 1, 1], SymInt groups=1, SymInt[]? input_size=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: the op reorders a CPU MkldnnCPU conv3d weight tensor into the oneDNN blocked layout expected by the mkldnn conv3d primitive; it only relocates existing values, so candidate and reference results are compared exactly and the input operand keeps its values. padding, stride, dilation, groups and, when supplied, input_size are passed as arguments to the native call; the supplied evidence ties the oneDNN weight descriptor to the group count dividing both channel dims and to kernel dims matching input_size, and input_size is the trailing optional positional argument that the frozen calls pass last (for example (1, 3, 16, 16, 16) alongside a (8, 3, 3, 3, 3) weight). The operand must be a rank>=3 MkldnnCPU tensor with dtype float32/bfloat16/float16/int8; dense operands, insufficient rank, zero/negative group counts and malformed kernel-dim parameter lists raise RuntimeError or TypeError, and autograd through the returned mkldnn tensor is not implemented. The other registered overload '.out' is keyword-only (out) and additionally aliases and mutates its buffer; this definition models the representative non-out overload only, and those overload-dependent effects remain owned by the original Gems pytest rather than being expressed here.
